changes.text: 居里夫妇把制备镭的方法毫无保留地公开，镭工业因此自由发展；他们自己却长期缺钱、缺场地。1921年赠镭之前，发起募捐、后来为居里夫人1923年出版的《皮埃尔·居里》一书写引言的梅洛尼去探访时，居里夫人的实验室仍设备不足；靠美国妇女募捐，居里夫人才得到一克镭。这是一笔两边都有分量的账。

The Curies published their method for preparing radium without reserve, and the radium industry grew freely on it. They themselves long went without money and without a proper workplace. When Meloney, who launched the subscription and later wrote the introduction to Pierre Curie, the book Marie Curie published in 1923, visited before the 1921 gift, Marie Curie's laboratory still lacked sufficient equipment, and a subscription raised by American women finally secured her a gram of radium. It is a ledger with weight on both sides.

一克镭的市价是十万美元。而制备镭的方法，是她和丈夫皮埃尔·居里多年前毫无保留地公开的，镭工业正靠它发展起来、高价卖货。公开了方法的她，实验室里那点镭当时只用于为医院提取射气。梅洛尼在美国发起募捐，希望借此让她把研究继续下去；后来，居里夫人1923年出版的《皮埃尔·居里》一书由梅洛尼写了引言。这笔账该书里两边都有记载：梅洛尼在引言里记下了市价和募捐，居里夫人自己在书中的自传笔记里算过放弃的那笔财富。

A gram of radium then sold for one hundred thousand dollars. The process for preparing it had been published years earlier, without reserve, by Marie Curie and her husband Pierre Curie, and the radium industry was now thriving on that very process and selling its product at a high price. She had helped give the method away, yet the radium in her laboratory was used at that time only for extracting emanations for hospital use. Meloney set out to raise a subscription in America to enable her to go on with her work; Meloney later wrote the introduction to Pierre Curie, the book Marie Curie published in 1923. That book records both sides of the account: Meloney's introduction notes the price and the subscription, and in the book's autobiographical notes Marie Curie reckons up the fortune she gave up.

后来有一次（书中未写年份），日内瓦方面来请皮埃尔：那里物质条件更好，还能过上近似乡居的宁静生活。按居里夫人的记述，这个决定很艰难，皮埃尔动了心。最后让他定下来不去的，是他们正对镭做的研究，他怕这样的变动打断它。此时，索邦P.C.N.（医科学生必修的物理、化学和博物课程）的物理教席正好空缺。他申请后，在一心想让他不必离开法国的庞加莱的影响下获聘；她则受托在塞夫尔的女子师范学校讲物理课。他们留在巴黎，收入增加了，工作却更难：皮埃尔要兼两处课，其中学生众多的P.C.N.教学让他非常疲惫。

At one point (the book gives no year), Geneva came calling for Pierre, offering material advantages and the opportunity of a life comparable in its tranquillity with that in the country. In Marie Curie's account the decision was a grave one, and Pierre was tempted. What finally settled it was the radium research itself, since he feared the interruption that such a change must involve. At this moment the chair of physics in the Sorbonne's P.C.N. course was vacant; this was the physics, chemistry and natural history course obligatory for students of medicine. He applied, and was appointed through the influence of Henri Poincaré, who was anxious to free him from the necessity of quitting France. Marie Curie was given charge of the physics lectures at the Normal School for Girls at Sèvres. They stayed in Paris and their income increased, but working conditions grew harder: Pierre was doing double teaching, and the P.C.N., with its very large number of students, fatigued him greatly.

还有一件事，她在书里两处都写到。按她的叙述，在她同意之下，皮埃尔·居里拒绝从发现中获取任何物质利益；他们没有申请版权（英译作「took no copyright」），把研究结果和制备镭的确切方法毫无保留地发表，来问的人也都得到答复。自传笔记里她又说了一遍：夫妇二人一贯不从发现中获取物质利益，方法从一开始就全部公开，没有申请专利（英译作「took out no patent」），也不在工业开发中保留任何好处。书里没写这个决定的日期。

There is something else she writes about in two places in the book. In Marie Curie's telling, and with her agreement, Pierre Curie refused to draw any material profit from the discovery. They also took no copyright (the English translation of the biography reads "We took no copyright"), published without reserve all the results of their research as well as the exact processes of the preparation of radium, and gave whatever information was asked of them. In the autobiographical notes she says it again: the two of them always refused to draw any material profit from the discovery, the process was published from the beginning, they took out no patent (the translation reads "We took out no patent"), and they reserved no advantage in any industrial exploitation. The book gives no date for the decision.

钱还是不够。受这次试验启发，法国实业家阿尔梅·德·利尔办起一座在当时看来很大胆的真正镭工厂，把产品卖给医生；医生们因各种研究的发表，已对镭的生物效应和可能的疗法产生兴趣。项目成功了，因为他能雇到居里夫妇训练过的人。镭从此有了稳定货源，价格很高：制备条件特殊，制镭所需矿物的价格又立刻上涨。书中接着写道，这位实业家不图回报地在他的工厂里给他们一小块工作地方和一部分所需费用。其余的钱有的是他们自己的，有的来自补助，最重要的一笔是1902年科学院给的20,000法郎。

The money was still short. Inspired by their attempt, a French industrialist, Armet de Lisle, took what seemed at that epoch the daring step of founding a veritable radium factory to furnish the product to physicians, whose interest in the biological effects of radium and its possible therapeutic applications had been aroused by the publication of various investigations. The project proved a success because he could employ men already trained by the Curies in the delicate processes of the manufacture. Radium was now regularly placed on sale, at a high price it is true, given the special conditions under which it had to be made and the immediate rise in the cost of the minerals necessary to its production. The book goes on to say that, in an entirely disinterested manner, the industrialist placed a little working place in his factory at their disposition, together with a part of the means necessary to use it. Other funds were added either by the Curies themselves or through subventions, the most important of which, accorded by the Academy of Sciences in 1902, amounted to 20,000 francs.
多年后，她在自传笔记里把账摊开。镭在矿石里含量极小，价格很高；镭又能治好多种疾病，所以制造利润很大。他们放弃的，是一笔本可留给子女的财富。更值得考虑的是许多朋友的反对：若当初保住权利，本可筹钱建一所像样的镭研究所，不必经历那些一直拖累两人、至今仍拖累她的难处。她承认朋友们的看法并非没有道理（英译作「not without reason」），但按英译本的措辞，她仍然认为他们做得对。

Years later, in the autobiographical notes, she laid out the rest of the ledger. Radium is found in minerals in very small quantities, so its price is very high, and the profits of its manufacture have been great, since the substance is used to cure a number of diseases. What they sacrificed in renouncing the exploitation of their discovery, then, was a fortune, one that could after them have gone to their children. And what was even more to be considered, she wrote, was the objection of many of their friends, who argued "not without reason" that if they had guaranteed their rights they could have had the financial means of founding a satisfactory Institute of Radium, without the difficulties that had been such a handicap to both of them and were still a handicap to her. She conceded the point and held her ground all the same; in the English translation: "Yet, I still believe that we have done right."

dispositions.rationale: dek中文把容易误指梅洛尼的“她的实验室”改为“居里夫人的实验室”，与英文 Marie Curie's laboratory 一致。

evidence.quote: Madame Curie's laboratory, although practically a new building, was without sufficient equipment

dispositions.rationale: dek英文 finally put a gram in Marie Curie's hands 改为 finally secured her a gram of radium，不再暗示她在仪式上亲手接过镭，与 hook 所述只交付金钥匙一致；中文“得到一克镭”本无此问题。

evidence.quote: The radium itself was not brought to the ceremony.

dispositions.rationale: 在第一次提到该书的 dek 中点明是居里夫人1923年出版的《皮埃尔·居里》，并把梅洛尼写成发起募捐、后来为该书写引言的人；hook.1 同样点明书名，并先交代她发起募捐，再说明她为该书写引言，后文改用“该书”。两种语言均写明1923，未添加证据以外的身份信息。

evidence.quote: to find ten women to subscribe ten thousand dollars each for the purchase of a gramme of radium

dispositions.rationale: 中文“为医科学生而设”改为“医科学生必修的物理、化学和博物课程”，并补上P.C.N.的课程说明；英文同步改为 course obligatory for students of medicine。

evidence.quote: the physics, chemistry and natural history course at the Sorbonne, obligatory for students of medicine

dispositions.rationale: 中文把「took no copyright」改为挂在“没有申请版权”之后，不再像是在解释“拒绝获利”；「took out no patent」改为挂在“没有申请专利”之后，去掉指代不清的“此处”。英文同步改写，分别说明 took no copyright 与 took out no patent，并标明是英译措辞。

evidence.quote: With my agreement he refused to draw any material profit from our discovery. We took no copyright
We took out no patent and we did not reserve any advantage in any industrial exploitation.

dispositions.rationale: E9 只用 he 指称，不再直接写作德·利尔，改为“书中接着写道，这位实业家……”。带有动机色彩的“出于好意”改为“不图回报”。英文同步改为 The book goes on to say that... the industrialist。

evidence.quote: In an entirely disinterested manner he placed at our disposition a little working place in his factory

dispositions.rationale: 英文在引语前加上 in the English translation，标明这是英译本措辞；中文同步注明“按英译本的措辞”，没有在中文里嵌入英文句子。

evidence.quote: Yet, I still believe that we have done right.
